output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows about 37 cases a month still reach confirmed-incident status, which matches the old baseline of about 38. Brackwater's analyst host (not the connector, which wrote no categories) has polled for cases carrying the SLA-warning flag every five minutes since 9 Sep. It then moved 47 confirmed cases to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" about 3h31m–3h42m after they opened. Those cases drop out of the containment-time and SLA metrics. That produces the 100% SLA figure, the faster containment time and the "bonus triggered" claim. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. The monitoring queue has grown from about 40 to 96 open cases. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents, have the in-house team and Halvard check containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Hold the renewal and request a written explanation from Brackwater. Service credits, at 2,500 per uncontained case, may well be owed, but confirm the contract terms and who made the decision before invoicing. Whether the 28 dropped rules created blind spots is still unknown, so review them separately. I am highly confident in the core finding.
